The Howard Hughes Medical Institute’s Janelia Research Campus is a pioneering research center in Ashburn, Virginia, where scientists pursue fundamental questions in the life sciences. Our integrated teams of biologists, computational scientists, and tool-builders innovate research practices and technologies to solve biology’s deepest mysteries. HHMI launched Janelia in 2006, establishing an intellectually enriching environment for scientists to do creative, collaborative, hands-on work. We share our methods, results, and tools with the scientific community.
  
  
**About The Project**
AI@HHMI is HHMI’s $500 million, 10-year investment in AI-driven science, embedding AI systems throughout every stage of research in labs across HHMI. HHMI is also partnering with frontier AI labs on scientific applications of AI (learn more).
  
  
At the heart of AI@HHMI is the Foundational Microscopy Image Analysis (MIA) project. Our goal is to build one of the world’s most comprehensive multimodal 3D/4D microscopy datasets, and use it to power a vision foundation model that accelerates discovery across the life sciences. Our current focus is reconstructing connectomes at scale from expansion microscopy (ExM) data generated by High-Throughput Connectomics, a sister AI@HHMI project.
  
  
**About The Role**
You will develop and deploy production-ready pipelines for segmenting and proofreading connectomes from expansion microscopy imaging across fly, zebrafish, and
*Danionella*
. You will scale reconstruction from individual datasets to hundreds or thousands of connectomes, working with large-scale volumetric data on a compute cluster with around 800 GPUs.
  
  
This role combines deep understanding of the underlying models with hands-on engineering and careful attention to reconstruction quality. You will work closely with microscopists, cell biologists, neuroscientists, and computer scientists so that models hold up on large, real-world data.
  
  
Your home is Scientific Computing, a department of about 35 AI, data, and software engineers, where you will report to department leadership. Your day-to-day work is directed by the AI Scientist who leads the MIA AI@HHMI project, a team of seven scientists and engineers. This is primarily an individual-contributor role, with potential opportunities to mentor junior engineers.
  
  
**What You Will Actually Do**

* Reconstruct connectomes at scale using our pre-trained segmentation models.
* Train and fine-tune models as new ground-truth data becomes available.
* Evaluate rigorously. Design and run rigorous model evaluations to measure and improve reconstruction quality.
* Optimize inference pipelines. Increase reconstruction throughput on GPU clusters.
* Build proofreading workflows. Build and support proofreading workflows (for example, integration with CAVE).
* Coordinate annotation. Coordinate manual annotation and proofreading efforts to improve training and evaluation data.
* Release your work. Release pipelines, models, and reconstructions to the broader scientific community, with a focus on reproducibility and downstream usability.
* Collaborate across disciplines. Advise stakeholders on data strategy and best practices, and potentially mentor junior engineers.

* You’ve taken ownership of the production reconstruction pipeline and run it end-to-end on new ExM datasets.
* You’ve measurably improved throughput or reconstruction accuracy against an agreed benchmark.
* You’ve delivered high-quality connectome segmentations that need minimal manual proofreading.

**What We Are Looking For**

* Production over prototype. You have trained and evaluated deep learning models (Transformers, U-Nets) for three or more years, ideally on 3D image data. You have also deployed them, with workflow orchestration and high-throughput processing on GPU clusters, using tools such as Kubernetes, Nextflow, or LSF.
* First-principles thinking. When a result moves, you can explain why. You know how architecture and regularization choices change performance, and you can design the experiment that tests your explanation.
* Fluent in the toolkit. You write strong Python in PyTorch or JAX. You are familiar with modern vision models such as DINOv3, SAM, Cellpose, and Vision Transformers.
